prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional ATFM+A-CDM; airports Meridian International(=Meridian Regional Airport), Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport. Modes (Airport Duty Manager=ADM declares; Business Rules Registry holds thresholds/latency/connection protection/gate compatibility/towing priority/stand reopening/turnaround margins): Normal Operations; Adverse Weather; Capacity Reduction State(extended metering horizon); Recovery Phase(Copperfin-approved; RFM authorizes exit; RFM balances restored arrival capacity, departure release, stand clearance); Contingency Fallback; Slot Compliance State; Winter(MBO confirms). Diversions in Recovery/Contingency. Actors: Regional Flow Manager=RFM(ranks diversions in Cedarbell), Airspace Sector Planner(may request Tactical Regulation Proposal), Military Airspace Liaison(flexible-use airspace adjustments), Tower Supervisor, ADM(Medical Diversion Notice), Ramp Control Lead & Ground Handling Dispatcher(confirm stand/towing/refuel/unloading via Handling Resource Planner; GHD uses tag list for baggage reconciliation before off-block readiness update), Aircraft Operator Rep, Airline Operations Coordinator(passenger/crew/maintenance/rotation impacts), Slot Coordinator(CTT/TOBT), Network Operations Liaison(alternates, swaps, crew legality, rebooking), Emergency Response Coordinator, Deicing Coordinator, Meteorology Briefing Officer=MBO(rapid forecasts), Data Governance Steward(role-restricted data). Cedarbell=Regional Flow Platform(treats exceptions as filtered, grouped, escalated before shared displays; exception record: flight, stand, milestone, recovery time, confidence, accountable role). Parts: Marlinstone=Demand Prediction Service; CAM=Capacity Assessment Module; Arrival Regulation Console; Blueharbor=Slot Allocation Engine(CTT, GDP, Pushback Window Token); Foxglove=Airport CDM Portal; Emberline=Departure Metering Service(CTT→Ironleaf=Tower Sequence Manager); Halcyon(logs push rationale); Runway Meters; Surface Surveillance Adapter; Apron Sensors; Ramp Movement Board; Gate Conflict Detector(diversion parking vs turnarounds/departure banks); Handling Resource Planner; Airline Interface Adapter; Sector Load Monitor; Lantern; Alert Distribution Hub(role-specific alerts); Digital Briefing Room(records rationale, priority, resources, recovery target in Collaborative Decision Log); Audit Event Ledger+Identity Access Service(traceability); Performance Analytics Warehouse(actual vs plan review). Rules: TOBT revised only when turnaround actor confirms; late baggage assessed vs connection criticality, loading closure, TOBT.

New part:
S521: The Airline Operations Coordinator confirms whether the aircraft can remain on plan, accept a short readiness deferral, or require a revised departure intent.
S522: The Handling Resource Planner assigns a severity level to the handler exception and suppresses duplicate updates while the accountable party is still working the same recovery action.
S523: The Ground Handling Dispatcher sends the Towbar Shortage Report when towbar availability cannot support the agreed pushback sequence.
S524: Towbar availability is escalated only when the missing equipment affects a flight inside the active departure planning horizon or blocks a higher-priority aircraft movement.
S525: The Ramp Movement Board displays the resulting constraint as a stand-level exception with a time band rather than as a continuous stream of equipment messages.
S526: Handler exceptions include staffing gaps, equipment unserviceability, access limitations, and service sequencing conflicts that could invalidate a readiness milestone.
S527: The Airport CDM Portal keeps detailed handler notes available to authorized users while the Common Situation Display shows only the flight impact, severity, and expected recovery window.
S528: This separation prevents local troubleshooting details from crowding the regional view used by the Regional Flow Manager, Tower Supervisor, and Slot Coordinator.
S529: The Alert Distribution Hub routes notifications according to severity, time to milestone, and subscribed operational role, rather than broadcasting every exception to all users.
S530: A baggage or handler exception becomes a coordination issue when it threatens the Target Off Block Time, the Calculated Takeoff Time, or an agreed runway metering sequence.
S531: At that point, the Airport CDM Portal prompts the accountable role to record the proposed mitigation in the Collaborative Decision Log.
S532: The Regional Flow Manager sees aggregated impact by departure bank, runway stream, and airline group instead of individual baggage or handler work items.
S533: The Slot Allocation Engine uses the sanitized readiness state when evaluating whether a regulated flight can keep its allocated departure opportunity.
S534: The Departure Metering Service applies exception status only after the Business Rules Registry threshold confirms that the condition is operationally material.
S535: Nightjar shall suppress handler-exception annotations for arriving flights unless the exception changes the Airport Acceptance Rate or a regulated arrival sequence.
S536: The Tower Sequence Manager receives a stable readiness indicator and an escalation flag, which allows tower planning to continue without interpreting ramp work details.
S537: The Audit Event Ledger records who raised, changed, acknowledged, or closed each escalated exception so that later review can distinguish data noise from operational decisions.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
